text:
maya: heads-up — nightly eval (03:05 UTC) on prod-dialogue-sanity dropped ~18% pass rate vs baseline. looks like a clustering of bad generations when prefix cache is used. attaching quick logs.

ben: ugh. can you paste the log excerpt?

maya: here —
```
[03:05:12] CACHE: prefix_lookup id=pf_8c3a5, key=sha1:ab12..., hit=true, collision=true, evicted=false
[03:05:12] RUNTIME: kv_cache_apply mismatch len=256 expected=240
[03:05:12] GENERATION: detokenized='How can I help you today?' -> 'How cam I help you today?'
```

sam: collision=true on prefix lookup looks suspicious. we've seen similar when two tenants share the same prefix hash space after quantized kernels changed padding. which model/config?

maya: model v2025-01-q4 (4-bit quant). nightly runner used batching policy 'adaptive-v2' with narrow windows. reproduces locally if I enable prefix cache + adaptive batching.

laura: did the nightly also run the new KV eviction heuristic? that was rolled to staging last week. if eviction timing changed, we could be hitting stale KV entries causing shifted generations.

maya: eviction heuristic=ttl-based (30s), yes. I toggled eviction to the old LRU locally and failures drop to 2%.

ben: interesting. so three variables: 4-bit quant, adaptive batching, and new ttl eviction. any single one sufficient to trigger?

maya: quick matrix:
- quant + old eviction + adaptive => 6% fail
- quant + ttl eviction + no adaptive => 4% fail
- quant + ttl eviction + adaptive => 18% fail (nightly)
- fp16 (no quant) + ttl eviction + adaptive => 1% fail

jin: that matrix points to an interaction between quant kernel padding (alignment), cache key construction, and batching interleaving. maybe buffered KV lengths differ and we compute key on raw bytes rather than normalized prefix length.

sam: can you dump the prefix key composition? i.e., what components go into sha1:ab12...

maya: sure — key = sha1(tenant_id|model_id|prefix_token_bytes|pad_len). suspect pad_len changed due to quant packing. snippet: ```compose_key(tenant, model, prefix, pad=align_to_32(tokens))```

laura:aha — if pad is included in the key, two logically identical prefixes with different pad_len will be treated distinct, but we see collision=true in the logs which means different keys hashed to same slot?

ben: collision flag is from the open-addressed table finding an occupied bucket with different tag. could be because we compacted tags from 64->32 bits in the new cache layout to save memory for Dedicated. that increases collision probability.

maya: we did that change in the infra patch rolled Feb 12. nightly runner picked a build after that.

sam: test suggestion: run nightly eval with the old cache-tag-width (64-bit) and keep TTL eviction + quant + adaptive batching. if failure drops, we pin the regression to tag-width change.

maya: running that now on a small subset (10 prompts). will post results ~03:30 UTC.

ci-bot: build #4121 deployed to nightly-runner (tag-width=64bit toggle enabled) — run started at 03:18 UTC.

laura: if it reproduces, I want an end-to-end differ run comparing token-level logits for failing prompts between the two cache layouts. that will tell if collision caused bit flips or just different cache entries returned.

maya: good plan. also adding a short term mitigator: skip prefix cache when model is quantized and adaptive batching is active. cheap flag while we debug.

ben: add the flag behind feature-flag and enable only for nightly to get more signal.

jin: FYI the quantized kernel padding change makes some KV buffer views point to the wrong offset if alignment math is off by 1. double-check get_kv_ptr() arithmetic. small off-by-one can explain deterministic but wrong tokens.

maya: result: 10-prompt run with 64-bit tags => failures down to 3/10 (30%) vs 8/10 before. still bad but improved. posting full logs in GH gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abcdef

sam: partial improvement means multiple factors. next: run with quantized->fp16 kernels (no quant) to confirm quant is dominant. also try disabling adaptive batching.

laura: I'll prepare an eval harness to diff logits and prefix key sequences per request. jin and ben, can you review cache-tag change?

ben: on it. i'll revert compact tag in a local branch and run the cache unit tests + a small stress harness.

jin: i'll audit alignment math in quant kernel.

maya: thanks everyone. will keep thread updated. tagging @eng-oncall just in case we need to roll back the infra change from Feb 12 to nightly images.

sam: nice triage. small asks: 1) open a short-lived tracking issue with the matrix and links 2) add a nightly-only feature-flag as maya suggested 3) schedule a quick sync if we see >10% failure in full nightly.

maya: created issue: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-1257 (matrix + gist + steps). feature-flag PR in progress.

jin: thumbs up.

ci-bot: nightly-runner build #4121 finished (03:29 UTC) — results: 10 prompts: 7 pass, 3 fail.

maya: note: failures are deterministic on this run and reproduce locally with same seed. next will be the logits diff.

laura: thanks. we'll follow up with root-cause writeup once we get the diffs. :mag:
